catalog_quote: 3.4 Acento. La consonante y la vocal de la última sílaba del tema se pronuncian ligeramente más largas y con mayor intensidad que en otras sílabas (E.V. Pike 1956: 70-71, Wagner Oviedo 2018: 227-228), lo que les confiere prominencia a las palabras, a lo que llamo acento. Las palabras gramaticales y los enclíticos no poseen prominencia. La palabra prosódica incluye todos los afijos, raíces, portamanteaux y enclíticos de un ítem léxico, a pesar de que los enclíticos no constituyen parte de la palabra léxica. [pp. 138-139] ... Aunque se necesita llevar a cabo estudios cuantitativos para verificar esta generalización, se incluye un ejemplo acústico para ilustrar esta tendencia de manera impresionista. [p. 139] ... Aún no se ha realizado un estudio fonético que precise la métrica de la palabra prosódica en el mazateco, pero se puede identificar la sílaba tónica por su mayor duración en comparación con las sílabas átonas ... En la plantilla propuesta, el acento recae en la última sílaba del complejo temático, justo antes del complejo enclítico. ... Los enclíticos no tienen acento tónico propio y se adjuntan prosódicamente a la palabra previa, sin posibilidad de enunciarse de manera independiente. [p. 143]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.translation: The consonant and the vowel of the last syllable of the stem are pronounced slightly longer and with greater intensity than in other syllables (E.V. Pike 1956: 70-71, Wagner Oviedo 2018: 227-228), which gives words prominence, which I call stress (acento). Grammatical words and enclitics have no prominence. [p. 138] ... In the proposed template, the stress falls on the last syllable of the thematic complex [= stem], right before the enclitic complex. [...] Enclitics have no stress of their own and attach prosodically to the preceding word, and cannot be uttered independently. [p. 143]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress (greater duration and intensity) falls on the last syllable of the stem, i.e. the final syllable of the lexical word before any enclitics; bisyllabic monomorphemic nouns are stressed on the final syllable ([nĩ³.ˈtʰĩ²] 'día', [lɑ¹.ˈꜜxu¹] 'piedra'), prefixed verbs on the root ([kwi¹.ꜜˈⁿt͡ʃa¹] 'va a hablar'), and roots keep the stress when enclitics follow ([ˈje¹.ɾa¹] 'su víbora'). Enclitics and grammatical words are unstressed. Because stems are root-final, the same fact is stated as root stress by Belmar 1892 p. 7 ('La raíz es la sílaba en que invariablemente reside el acento'); a 'morphologically determined' reading is equally defensible. Stress conditions allophony: /e/ -> [je] only in stressed syllables, [l] pretonic/tonic vs [ɾ] post-tonic, full oralization of nasals post-tonically.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed by Klint. Belmar 1892 p. 7: words formed by juxtaposition (compounds) carry two or more accents, one per major constituent.
new_statements.exceptions: Grammatical words (e.g. demonstrative [β̞ɑ¹], relativizer [ʃi²]) and enclitics have no prominence (Klint 2025 p. 138-139); Belmar 1892 p. 7 says some particles lose their accent when attached to the following word, and lists paroxytone words (káni 'mono', naña 'perro', natse 'mosca') besides oxytones and 'perispomena', while denying proparoxytones. Klint stresses that no quantitative phonetic study of the metrical structure exists yet; the description is impressionistic (pp. 139, 143).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the prosodic word = stem (prefixes + roots + derivational/compositional suffixes) + enclitics; stress sits on the last syllable of the stem, so it is final within the lexical word but non-final within the prosodic word when enclitics follow. Language is tonal (three level tones A/M/B); stressed syllables may carry two tones (contour), unstressed ones only one (pp. 138-139, tone chapter). Evidence from isolated words, elicited phrases and Bible-translation corpus; an acoustic phrase example (Fig. 34, p. 139).
new_statements.identity_note: All three Klint sources describe the Mazatec of Mazatlán Villa de Flores itself (speakers from Barrio del Corral/Nga̱súnchá and Barrio Guadalupe; ISO vmz = maza1296; INALI 'mazateco del suroeste'). Belmar 1892 (Glottolog's grammar sketch for maza1296) does not state where its data were collected; it only names San Cristóbal Mazatlán as the town that gave the language its name. Note: Glottolog ref 441837 (Juárez García 2005) attached to maza1296 is a Mazahua (El Depósito) thesis, not Mazatec — a misfiled record.

tone_statements.quote: El tono alto se escribirá con la tilde (acento agudo) á ... Para el mazateco la escritura del tono es tan importante como el de las vocales o consonantes (todos son fonemas de la lengua). ... Las variantes que escriben tres tonos son Mazatlán, Chilchotla, Tlacotepec, Independencia, Ayautla, Chiquihuitlán, Ixcatlán, Jalapa y Soyaltepec.
tone_statements.translation: High tone will be written with the acute accent á ... For Mazatec, writing tone is as important as writing the vowels or consonants (all are phonemes of the language). ... The variants that write three tones are Mazatlán, Chilchotla, Tlacotepec, Independencia, Ayautla, Chiquihuitlán, Ixcatlán, Jalapa and Soyaltepec.

sources.note: §8 Acento, p. 5: 'La consonante y la vocal de la última sílaba del tema se pronuncian de manera ligeramente más larga que otras sílabas (E. Pike 1956:70-71) y con más intensidad (Beal 2011:161), dándole prominencia en la palabra; lo que llamamos acento. Las palabras gramaticales y los enclíticos no tienen prominencia.' sources.note: Tone is phonemic and written obligatorily: high tone = acute accent (á), 'semialto' = grave accent (only in four-tone variants), mid tone unmarked (a), low tone = underline (a̱). Variants are split into those writing four tones (Coyomeapan, Huehuetlán, Cuaunecuiltitla.., Huautla, Tenango) and those writing three tones: Mazatlán, Chilchotla, Tlacotepec, Independencia, Ayautla, Chiquihuitlán, Ixcatlán, Jalapa, Soyaltepec - illustrated with the Mazatlán triplet xá 'trabajo' / xa 'felino' / xa̱ 'sucio, borroso, neblina' (alphabet page: xín 'tlayudo' / xin 'clavo' / xi̱n 'hombre').
